judgment.rationale: Second SFI (Class-3, rank 2, under C-2.3 'applies the four basic operations ... to solve real-life problems') is 'Constructs stories involving the operations', with its LC 'Construct stories (word problems) involving the four basic operations'. First SFI (Class-5, rank 4, under C-2.4 money transactions) is 'Solving problems involving money using four basic operations (bills) as needed and estimation', with LCs solving bill/money word problems by addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and estimating amounts. Composing word-problem stories for each of the four operations establishes the operation-situation semantics that a learner must recognise to select and apply the appropriate operation(s) in Class-5 real-life money/bill problems, which further extend the work with a money context, multi-step bills and estimation. Direction is lower rank (Class-3) to higher rank (Class-5), matching the permitted second_to_first. Both endpoints share only Curricular Goal CG-2 and sit under different competencies, and part of each endpoint's source evidence is truncated, so support is judged from the visible statement text and Learning Components rather than shared ancestry or lexical overlap alone; hence moderate confidence.

judgment.rationale: Both Content SFIs sit under Competency C-1.3 ('Groups objects using two or more attributes or properties') within CG-1, and both are classification tasks, but they differ substantively in the attribute basis. The Class-1 item (rank 0) classifies concrete objects by observable behavioural features (rolling, sliding), while the Class-2 item (rank 1) classifies 2-D shapes by formal geometric properties (number of sides and corners), as confirmed by the LCs ('classify objects based on features such as rolling and sliding' vs 'classify 2-D shapes based on their properties such as number of sides and corners'). This is an extension from informal, perceptual/behavioural sorting of objects to property-based classification of abstract geometric figures, so proficiency in the earlier classification skill supports success in the later one; direction follows the lower-to-higher Class coordinate (Class-1 -> Class-2). Shared wording and page proximity alone were not treated as sufficient; the pair-specific shift in classification criteria carries the judgment. Ancestor Competency and Curricular Goal nodes lack developmental coordinates and were used only as context.

judgment.rationale: Class-4 Content (rank 3) is 'Division of a two digit number by a single digit number, division of a three digit number by a single digit numbers' with LCs for dividing two- and three-digit numbers; Class-5 Content (rank 4) is 'Understands powers of 10 seen so far, and all four operations on them' with LCs including 'Divide powers of 10', 'Multiply powers of 10', add and subtract powers of 10. Both sit under Competency C-2.3 (applying the four operations) and CG-2 (fluency with whole numbers, place value). Established procedural division fluency with two/three-digit dividends plausibly supports the later, broader work of carrying out all four operations on powers of 10, which extends operational skill to place-value-structured numbers; direction is lower-to-higher rank as permitted. Evidence is limited: only one shared operation token ('division'/'divide'), and the Class-5 statement's emphasis on place-value understanding of powers of 10 is only partly dependent on prior division work, so confidence is moderate. judgment.rationale: Class-4 Content 'Skip counting and construction of multiplication tables of 6, 7, 8 and 9' (LCs: skip count by 6-9; construct the multiplication tables of 6-9) and Class-3 Content 'Constructs stories involving the operations' (LC: construct stories/word problems involving the four basic operations) both sit under Competency C-2.3 (relationships among operations, applying the four operations to real-life problems) and CG-2 (fluency with the four arithmetical operations and number facts). producer_judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content SFIs about directional/spatial language. The second (Class-2, rank 1, under C-1.13 computational thinking) has children frame instructions using relative and cardinal directions (straight, right, left, upward, downward, east, west, north, south), per its LCs. The first (Class-3, rank 2, under C-3.2 'Describes location and movement... concept of a map') extends this to using directions to orient oneself and to move from one place to another, i.e. applying the same directional vocabulary to actual self-orientation and navigation rather than only verbalising instructions. This is a substantive extension from stating direction-based instructions to enacting orientation and movement, so Class-2 proficiency supports success at Class-3; the permitted lower-to-higher direction (second_to_first) matches the resolved Class coordinates. Evidence limits: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry merge/no-coordinate context, so the judgment rests on the bounded description, LC, and coordinate evidence only.
